stories.title: AI spending gets repriced
stories.summary: Investors now want proof that AI spending pays back in cash, so money is leaving AI hardware and, as of Oct 29, software too.
stories.changed: Nov 24: Monday's AI bounce did not get a second day (HPE margin warning, chips sold), but Dell's record AI orders after the close argue demand is still there.

thesis.what: Since early October the AI-hardware groups (chip equipment, optical, AI servers, custom chips, memory, neoclouds, data-center power) fell about 18% over 20 sessions while IT services, enterprise software and steady consumer names rose about 10%: a 28-point swing. On Oct 22 the S&P 500 fell 1.2% but the equal-weight S&P rose 0.7%: the money moved, it didn't leave.
thesis.why: Two worries feed each other. **Cost:** Meta announced non-voting shares to help fund its AI spending and fell 5%; Tesla cut capex; Lam Research guided below consensus ([Korea Times](https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/world/20261023/wall-street-sinks-as-nasdaq-falls-over-2-on-ai-cost-worries), [Investrade](https://investrade.com/market-review-october-22-2026/)). **Financing:** hot CPI pushed the 10-year to 5.26% and CoreWeave's credit spread past 1,000 bp, so borrowing to build data centers got expensive ([TradingKey](https://www.tradingkey.com/analysis/stocks/us-stocks/262218623-us-premarket-tsmc-record-profit-chip-stocks-fall-nvidia-micron-ppi-tradingkey)). Funding is the newest strain: Meta plans to raise up to $95B, starting with $35B in stock ([MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/news/wall-st-rises-as-anthropic-s-ipo-filing-sharpens-focus-on-ai-trade-ce785cdcdd8ff22d)), and Anthropic's filing adds a large new AI listing to the supply.
thesis.how: Funds were crowded in AI hardware after a huge run. When the spending story wobbles they trim those winners first and park the money in businesses that grow without AI capex (software, IT services, staples). The giants' weight drags the S&P down while the average stock holds up.
thesis.real: Still a seesaw. Monday the sold-hardest AI groups ripped; today they gave much of it back while the average stock rose. The price check reads wobbling: the 20-day call holds, the last 5 days are mixed.
thesis.confirm: Confirm: AI hardware fails to hold gains on Dell's strong report (Nov 25), which says investors doubt the profit, not the demand. Break: Dell holds up and chips follow for two or more days. Then PCE inflation (Nov 25) and the Fed on Dec 9.

thesis.confirm: Confirm: biotech holds its gains on a day AI hardware rallies, and more deals or strong data follow. Break: the groups give back today's move within a few sessions.

thesis.real: Early: one earnings week. Burlington guided Q4 comps only 0–2%, and homebuilder and consumer-confidence data show stretched lower-income shoppers. Treat it as a rotation home for money, not a boom.
thesis.confirm: **Confirms:** strong Black Friday / Cyber Monday reads, off-price holding gains into December, more retailers raising guidance. **Breaks:** weak holiday sales data or off-price giving back the earnings gaps.

stories.title: AI credit squeeze: data-center debt is the tell
stories.summary: Lenders are pulling back from AI data-center debt; the stocks most dependent on borrowing (neoclouds, Oracle) bounce hardest and fail fastest, and credit hasn't confirmed any bounce yet.
stories.changed: Nov 24: opened. Monday's neocloud bounce (+20%) was mostly gone today (−11%) while HYG/IEI barely moved; credit is the light to watch.

thesis.what: The cost of insuring AI borrowers against default has hit records (Oracle five-year CDS 288 bp, CoreWeave past 1,000 bp in mid-October), single-B junk spreads widened to 367 bp in the Nov 5 selloff, and banks are now stress-testing data-center cash flows and contract cancellation clauses. On the dashboard: neoclouds −22% since the Nov 4 thrust eve; HYG/IEI −1.1% over 5 sessions and just 0.1% off its 25-day low.
thesis.why: The build-out needs far more money than hyperscaler cash flow covers; the gap is filled by bonds, private credit and data-center ABS. When lenders get picky, the borrowers that need the next loan to finish a project (neoclouds, Oracle's leased campuses) get repriced first; cash-rich hyperscalers much less.
thesis.how: Two speeds. Cash-funded giants (Amazon, Microsoft, Alphabet) hold up better; debt-funded builders and tenants (CoreWeave, Nebius, Oracle, data-center developers) swing hardest both ways. Credit spreads move before equity confirms.
thesis.real: Real and documented in bond and CDS markets, but concentrated: broad junk (HYG/IEI) is only ~3.6% off its 1-year high while SPY was 11.5% off at the low. It explains why AI bounces fail fast; it does not yet look like a general credit crunch.
thesis.confirm: **Easing:** HYG/IEI rising for a week, neoclouds holding a bounce for 3+ sessions, Oracle CDS headlines turning. **Worsening:** HYG/IEI under its Nov 20 low (0.6626), a pulled data-center bond deal or a neocloud financing miss, Oracle downgrade talk.

stories.title: Gulf attacks keep oil above $100

thesis.what: Energy groups (refiners, shale, integrated oil, tankers, drillers) are up about 8% over 20 sessions while airlines fell 10%: an 18-point swing, though the last 5 days stalled.
thesis.why: Houthi attacks on Saudi sites (Oct 9, Oct 12, Oct 22) and reported attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz (Oct 14) put supply at risk; Brent went from $97.92 to $111.88 ([Nation Thailand](https://www.nationthailand.com/news/40070809), [Euronews](https://www.euronews.com/2026/10/14/oil-prices-rise-after-reported-attacks-on-ships-in-strait-of-hormuz), [Investrade](https://investrade.com/morning-preview-october-22-2026/)).
thesis.how: A supply scare lifts crude, and when fuel prices rise faster than crude (crack spread up) refiners earn the most; when crude outruns fuel, producers win. Airlines pay for the fuel. Higher oil also feeds inflation, which ties this story to rates.
thesis.real: Wobbling: the 20-day call is right but the last 5 days went against it (refiners down on Valero's earnings day despite the crack +4%). That's crowding in a group that roughly doubled since June. Oct 23: oil jumped again and Integrated Oil rose, while refiners dipped, so crude is leading and the refining margin is not.
thesis.confirm: Confirm: more attacks or supply losses keep Brent over $110 and refiners hold their gains through earnings. Break: a ceasefire or diplomatic progress drops Brent back under $100, or refiners keep falling while the crack rises (distribution). Oct 27: talks are the risk; a deal would take oil lower, new attacks would reverse today's drop.

stories.title: Making room for Anthropic: the IPO supply test
stories.summary: A record ~$90B Anthropic offering prices Nov 18. The theory says funds sell AI winners to pay for it; the one pattern the data shows (SpaceX, n=1) is that stand-in stocks get dumped once the real one trades.
stories.changed: Resolved Nov 24: the story's own break test fired - after pricing, AI hardware kept falling and Anthropic closed under its $83 issue price, so the selling was about AI itself, not making room for the IPO. Followed by the AI credit squeeze story.

thesis.what: Anthropic is selling 825M shares at $70–78 (up to $64.4B) plus a $26B private placement at the IPO price, about $90B in all, more than SpaceX's record $75B. Since its public filing on Oct 26 the dashboard's AI-hardware basket is **−7.6% vs SPY** (16th percentile of all 14-session windows), the 50 crowded momentum winners **−8.2%** (14th pct) and NVDA **−23%**, while AVGO is +7% and AMZN (a big Anthropic owner) +8.5%.
thesis.why: New stock has to be paid for. Research on 254 IPOs found that stocks most like a big new issue fall relative to others in the IPO month, more so when the IPO is bigger ([Braun & Larrain, Review of Financial Studies 2009](https://www.bostonfed.org/-/media/Documents/Workingpapers/PDF/wp0604.pdf)), though the authors note one IPO rarely moves a large developed market. This one is unusual: it is [about six times oversubscribed](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/anthropics-ipo-is-about-six-times-oversubscribed-bloomberg-news-reports-5023345), so funds want more than they'll get.
thesis.how:
Two separate mechanisms. **Funding:** managers trim crowded winners to raise cash for an allocation. **Proxy swap:** before the real stock exists, money crowds into stand-ins (for SpaceX, the space stocks); once the real one trades, the stand-ins get sold to buy it. The SpaceX test supports the second, not the first.

**The Anthropic stand-ins** (the names bought as "Anthropic exposure" before ANT exists; ranked by how much of each is Anthropic):
- **SKM (SK Telecom):** its ~$2.7B stake is about 20% of its market value, the purest listed proxy ([Nasdaq](https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/anthropic-ipo-what-it-means-wall-street)).
- **VCX** (closed-end venture fund): Anthropic was ~21% of its value at listing ([Financial Samurai](https://www.financialsamurai.com/?p=295793)). **−9.2% vs SPY** since Oct 26.
- **DXYZ (Destiny Tech100):** ~14% in Anthropic via special-purpose vehicles as of Nov 2 ([NerdWallet](https://www.nerdwallet.com/investing/news/can-you-buy-anthropic-stock)).
- **ZM (Zoom):** a ~$3.1B stake, about 11% of its market value ([AJ Bell](https://www.ajbell.co.uk/group/news/how-investors-can-gain-exposure-anthropic-it-joins-stock-market)). **+3.2% vs SPY** since Oct 26.
- **Funds with a slice:** Corgi MANGOS ETF (MN, ~9%), BlackRock BST (~7%) and BSTZ (~6%) ([Longbridge / MarketWatch](https://longbridge.com/en/news/303425610)).
- **Big owners, small slice:** AMZN (stake ~2% of its value, **+8.5% vs SPY**), GOOGL (**−5.2%**), CRM (**−10.6%**) ([Nasdaq](https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/anthropic-ipo-what-it-means-wall-street)). Too diluted to swing on the IPO alone.
The SpaceX pattern says the high-percentage ones (SKM, VCX, DXYZ, ZM) are the ones most at risk of being sold once ANT trades.
thesis.real: Mostly not shown to be the cause. AI hardware bounced on Monday on Nvidia's CEO news, not on the deal being done, and fell again today. If it is still weak after Nov 25 (five sessions after pricing), the selling was about AI itself and this story should close. *Written by Claude, which Anthropic makes: weigh accordingly.*
thesis.confirm: **Proves the funding story:** AI hardware and the crowded winners bounce within ~5 sessions after the Nov 18 pricing (after SpaceX, AI hardware ran +9% vs SPY in 5 sessions before fading to −13% by 20). **Breaks it:** they keep falling after the deal is done, which means the selling was about AI itself. **Proxy test:** stocks bought as 'Anthropic exposure' lag after ANT starts trading Nov 19. NVDA reports Nov 17, the day before pricing, so that night can swamp everything.
